summary.short: Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone promoting the AI industry, in force 1 November 2022. They set municipal coordination and promotion measures for research, infrastructure, data and applications, establish an AI ethics committee, require risk-based supervision, and prohibit listed conduct by AI research and application organisations.
summary.long: The Regulations, adopted by the Standing Committee of the 7th Shenzhen Municipal People's Congress on 30 August 2022 and in force from 1 November 2022, promote the AI industry in Shenzhen Municipality and set governance rules for AI research and application. The municipal competent industry authorities implement and supervise the AI industry within the municipal administrative area. Chapters II to V set promotional measures, including support for basic research and funding, public data resources and data sharing, AI data centres subject to higher energy efficiency standards, testing and certification platforms, application scenarios, and talent and investment support. Article 44 allows low-risk AI products without national or local standards to be piloted. Article 65 establishes a municipal AI ethics committee. Article 66 requires classified supervision: high-risk applications face pre-process evaluation and risk warning, while medium- and low-risk applications face pre-process disclosure and post-process tracking. Article 71 requires algorithms used in public decision-making to be explained to the public. Article 72 requires ethical safety reviews and risk assessments and prohibits, among other acts, endangering national security or public interests, infringing privacy, discriminating against users, and price discrimination based on user habits. Violations are to be punished or investigated under the Civil Code and related laws.

relations.target_text: Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China
relations.note: Article 72 states that violators of its prohibited-acts list are punished or investigated in accordance with the Civil Code, together with relevant laws on national security, personal information and consumer rights. The Civil Code is named but not otherwise described in this text.

evidence.quote: in accordance with the Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China and relevant laws and regulations on national security

notes: Source is an English translation supplied in the document; no Chinese original was provided. No enabling statute is named. Art. 1 cites only 'relevant laws and administrative regulations' and Art. 65 cites 'relevant national provisions on AI governance', so no legal_basis relation is recorded. Art. 72 sets out prohibitions but no sanctions; the text refers violations to other laws. Art. 66 says measures for tiered supervision 'shall be formulated separately' by the municipal government; these are not in this text. thresholds.note: The text contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Article 66 sorts AI applications into high, medium and low risk without numeric criteria and delegates the supervision measures to a separate municipal measure, which is not a numeric threshold. Dates (Art. 73), annual reporting timing (Art. 62) and stated objectives are not thresholds.
